en.L: burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
en.B: burn for burn, gash for gash, welt for welt.
en.R: a burn for a burn, a cut for a cut, a bruise for a bruise.

es.L: quemadura por quemadura, herida por herida, golpe por golpe.
es.B: quemadura por quemadura, tajo por tajo, verdugón por verdugón.
es.R: una quemadura por una quemadura, un corte por un corte, un moretón por un moretón.

fr.L: brûlure pour brûlure, blessure pour blessure, meurtrissure pour meurtrissure.
fr.B: brûlure pour brûlure, entaille pour entaille, zébrure pour zébrure.
fr.R: une brûlure pour une brûlure, une coupure pour une coupure, un bleu pour un bleu.

sw.L: kuungua kwa kuungua, jeraha kwa jeraha, mchubuko kwa mchubuko.
sw.B: jeraha la moto kwa jeraha la moto, mpasuko kwa mpasuko, alama ya pigo kwa alama ya pigo.
sw.R: kuchomeka kwa kuchomeka, kukatwa kwa kukatwa, uvimbe kwa uvimbe.

decisions.choice: burning, wound, stripe: every kind of bodily injury
decisions.reason: The three words name a burn, an open wound, and the welt or bruise a blow leaves. With verse 24 they cover injuries of every kind.

decisions.choice: gash, welt (Balanced); cut, bruise (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "wound" and "stripe".

source.text: וְכִֽי־יַכֶּ֨ה אִ֜ישׁ אֶת־עֵ֥ין עַבְדּ֛וֹ אֽוֹ־אֶת־עֵ֥ין אֲמָת֖וֹ וְשִֽׁחֲתָ֑הּ לַֽחָפְשִׁ֥י יְשַׁלְּחֶ֖נּוּ תַּ֥חַת עֵינֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And when strikes a man the eye of his male slave or the eye of his female slave and destroys it, as free he will let him go in place of his eye.

en.L: And when {{gender:someone|a man}} strikes the eye of {{gender:their|his}} male slave or the eye of {{gender:their|his}} female slave and destroys it, {{gender:they|he}} will let [the slave] go free in place of [the] eye.
en.B: If {{gender:an owner|a man}} hits a slave, male or female, in the eye and blinds that eye, the slave goes free as payment for the lost eye.
en.R: If {{gender:an owner|a man}} hits a slave, man or woman, and blinds one of the slave's eyes, the owner must let the slave go free because of the lost eye.

es.L: Y cuando {{gender:alguien|un hombre}} golpee el ojo de su esclavo o el ojo de su esclava y lo destruya, lo dejará ir libre a cambio del ojo.
es.B: Si {{gender:un amo|un hombre}} golpea a un esclavo o a una esclava en el ojo y le hace perder ese ojo, el esclavo quedará libre como pago por el ojo perdido.
es.R: Si {{gender:un amo|un hombre}} golpea a un esclavo o a una esclava y le hace perder un ojo, el amo debe dejar libre al esclavo por el ojo perdido.

fr.L: Et quand {{gender:quelqu’un|un homme}} frappe l’œil de son esclave homme ou l’œil de son esclave femme et le détruit, il le laissera aller libre à la place de l’œil.
fr.B: Si {{gender:un maître|un homme}} frappe un esclave, homme ou femme, à l’œil et lui fait perdre cet œil, l’esclave sera libéré en compensation de l’œil perdu.
fr.R: Si {{gender:un maître|un homme}} frappe un esclave, homme ou femme, et le rend aveugle d’un œil, le maître doit laisser l’esclave partir libre à cause de l’œil perdu.

sw.L: Na mtu akilipiga jicho la mtumwa wake wa kiume au jicho la mtumwa wake wa kike na kuliharibu, atamwacha aende huru badala ya jicho [lake].
sw.B: Mtu akimpiga mtumwa wake, mwanamume au mwanamke, jichoni na kulipofusha jicho hilo, mtumwa huyo ataachiliwa huru kama malipo ya jicho lililopotea.
sw.R: Mtu akimpiga mtumwa wake, mwanamume au mwanamke, na kumpofusha jicho moja, lazima amwache mtumwa huyo aende huru kwa sababu ya jicho alilopoteza.

decisions.choice: set free in place of the eye: the slave's injury is repaid with freedom
decisions.reason: The law of equivalence (verses 23-25) applies to slaves too, but the payment is the slave's freedom. An owner who maims a slave loses the slave.

decisions.choice: destroys it: ruins its sight
decisions.reason: The verb means to ruin or destroy; here the eye is blinded.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought, sold, owned or released: the injured slave is set free (m1).

source.text: וְאִם־שֵׁ֥ן עַבְדּ֛וֹ אֽוֹ־שֵׁ֥ן אֲמָת֖וֹ יַפִּ֑יל לַֽחָפְשִׁ֥י יְשַׁלְּחֶ֖נּוּ תַּ֥חַת שִׁנּֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And if the tooth of his male slave or the tooth of his female slave he knocks out, as free he will let him go in place of his tooth.

en.L: And if the tooth of {{gender:their|his}} male slave or the tooth of {{gender:their|his}} female slave {{gender:they knock|he knocks}} out, {{gender:they|he}} will let [the slave] go free in place of [the] tooth.
en.B: The same holds for a tooth: a slave, man or woman, whose tooth the owner knocks out is to be freed for the tooth.
en.R: If an owner knocks out a slave's tooth, the slave goes free because of that tooth too.

es.L: Y si hace caer el diente de su esclavo o el diente de su esclava, lo dejará ir libre a cambio del diente.
es.B: Lo mismo vale para un diente: el esclavo o la esclava a quien su amo le haga saltar un diente quedará libre por ese diente.
es.R: Si un amo le rompe un diente a un esclavo, el esclavo también queda libre por ese diente.

fr.L: Et s’il fait tomber la dent de son esclave homme ou la dent de son esclave femme, il le laissera aller libre à la place de la dent.
fr.B: Il en va de même pour une dent : l’esclave, homme ou femme, à qui le maître casse une dent sera libéré pour cette dent.
fr.R: Si un maître casse une dent à un esclave, l’esclave part libre à cause de cette dent aussi.

sw.L: Na akiling'oa jino la mtumwa wake wa kiume au jino la mtumwa wake wa kike, atamwacha aende huru badala ya jino [lake].
sw.B: Ndivyo ilivyo pia kwa jino: mtumwa, mwanamume au mwanamke, ambaye bwana wake amemng'oa jino, ataachiliwa huru kwa ajili ya jino hilo.
sw.R: Bwana akimng'oa mtumwa jino, mtumwa huyo pia anakwenda huru kwa sababu ya jino hilo.

decisions.choice: even a tooth: any lasting harm frees the slave
decisions.reason: A tooth is a small loss beside an eye. Even so, an owner who knocks one out must set the slave free. The law protects slaves from abuse by their owners.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought, sold, owned or released: the injured slave is set free (m1).

source.text: וְכִֽי־יִגַּ֨ח שׁ֥וֹר אֶת־אִ֛ישׁ א֥וֹ אֶת־אִשָּׁ֖ה וָמֵ֑ת סָק֨וֹל יִסָּקֵ֜ל הַשּׁ֗וֹר וְלֹ֤א יֵאָכֵל֙ אֶת־בְּשָׂר֔וֹ וּבַ֥עַל הַשּׁ֖וֹר נָקִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And when gores an ox a man or a woman and he dies, surely will be stoned the ox, and not will be eaten its flesh, and the owner of the ox [is] free.

en.L: And when an ox gores a man or a woman so that [the person] dies, the ox will surely be stoned, and its flesh will not be eaten, but the owner of the ox [is] free [of guilt].
en.B: When an ox kills a man or a woman with its horns, the animal is to be stoned and its meat left uneaten. Its owner, though, bears no guilt.
en.R: Suppose an ox kills a man or a woman with its horns. People must kill the ox by throwing stones at it, and no one may eat its meat. But the owner is not to blame.

es.L: Y cuando un buey cornee a un hombre o a una mujer y [la persona] muera, el buey será ciertamente apedreado, y no se comerá su carne, pero el dueño del buey [quedará] libre [de culpa].
es.B: Cuando un buey mate a un hombre o a una mujer con sus cuernos, el animal será apedreado y no se comerá su carne. Su dueño, en cambio, no tendrá culpa.
es.R: Supón que un buey mata a un hombre o a una mujer con sus cuernos. La gente debe matar al buey tirándole piedras, y nadie puede comer su carne. Pero el dueño no tiene la culpa.

fr.L: Et quand un bœuf encorne un homme ou une femme et que [la personne] meurt, le bœuf sera certainement lapidé, et sa chair ne sera pas mangée, mais le propriétaire du bœuf [sera] quitte.
fr.B: Quand un bœuf tue un homme ou une femme d’un coup de cornes, l’animal sera lapidé et l’on ne mangera pas sa viande. Son propriétaire, lui, ne sera pas coupable.
fr.R: Imagine qu’un bœuf tue un homme ou une femme avec ses cornes. Les gens doivent tuer le bœuf en lui jetant des pierres, et personne ne doit manger sa viande. Mais le propriétaire n’est pas responsable.

sw.L: Na ng'ombe akimpiga pembe mwanamume au mwanamke, naye [mtu huyo] akafa, kwa hakika ng'ombe huyo atapigwa mawe, wala nyama yake haitaliwa, lakini mwenye ng'ombe [hana] hatia.
sw.B: Ng'ombe akimuua mwanamume au mwanamke kwa pembe zake, mnyama huyo atapigwa mawe na nyama yake haitaliwa. Lakini mwenye ng'ombe hana hatia.
sw.R: Tuseme ng'ombe amemuua mwanamume au mwanamke kwa pembe zake. Watu lazima wamuue ng'ombe huyo kwa kumpiga mawe, na mtu yeyote asile nyama yake. Lakini mwenye ng'ombe hana lawama.

decisions.choice: the ox will be stoned and not eaten: the animal answers for a human life
decisions.reason: God requires a reckoning for human blood, even from an animal (Genesis 9:5). The ox is put to death by stoning, and its meat may not be eaten, since it has taken a life.

decisions.choice: free: not guilty
decisions.reason: The owner had no reason to expect the ox to gore, so he bears no guilt. Verse 29 gives the case where he had been warned.

decisions.choice: ox: a head of cattle
decisions.reason: The word is used of a single bull, cow or ox, especially as a working animal.

decisions.choice: "bœuf" for the ox (shor), "encorner" for gore
decisions.reason: "Shor" is a head of cattle used for work, which French calls "bœuf"; "taureau" would narrow it to a bull. "Encorner" is the ordinary verb for an animal's goring. The same words through verse 36.

decisions.choice: "ng'ombe" for the ox (shor), "kupiga pembe" for gore
decisions.reason: "Shor" is a head of cattle, ox, bull or cow, and the law covers any of them; "ng'ombe" says that, where "fahali" would limit it to a bull. The same words through verse 36.

source.text: וְאִ֡ם שׁוֹר֩ נַגָּ֨ח ה֜וּא מִתְּמֹ֣ל שִׁלְשֹׁ֗ם וְהוּעַ֤ד בִּבְעָלָיו֙ וְלֹ֣א יִשְׁמְרֶ֔נּוּ וְהֵמִ֥ית אִ֖ישׁ א֣וֹ אִשָּׁ֑ה הַשּׁוֹר֙ יִסָּקֵ֔ל וְגַם־בְּעָלָ֖יו יוּמָֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And if an ox prone to gore it [was] from yesterday [and] the third day, and it was warned to its owner, and not he guarded it, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox will be stoned, and also its owner will be put to death.

en.L: But if the ox [was] prone to gore from yesterday [and] the third day, and its owner was warned, and he did not keep it in, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox will be stoned, and its owner also will be put to death.
en.B: It is different if the ox was known to gore before. If its owner had been told of the danger and still failed to keep it in, and it then kills a man or a woman, the ox must be stoned, and the owner too must die.
en.R: But maybe the ox has attacked people with its horns before, and the owner was warned about it but did not keep it locked up. Then if it kills a man or a woman, the ox must be stoned, and the owner also deserves death.

es.L: Pero si el buey [era] dado a cornear desde ayer [y] el tercer día, y a su dueño se le advirtió, y no lo guardó, y mata a un hombre o a una mujer, el buey será apedreado, y también se dará muerte a su dueño.
es.B: Es distinto si se sabía que el buey ya embestía antes. Si a su dueño se le había advertido del peligro y aun así no lo tuvo encerrado, y luego mata a un hombre o a una mujer, el buey será apedreado, y también el dueño será condenado a muerte.
es.R: Pero tal vez el buey ya ha atacado a la gente con sus cuernos, y el dueño fue advertido pero no lo mantuvo encerrado. Entonces, si mata a un hombre o a una mujer, el buey debe ser apedreado, y el dueño también merece la muerte.

fr.L: Mais si le bœuf [avait] l’habitude d’encorner depuis hier [et] le troisième jour, et que son propriétaire a été averti, et qu’il ne l’a pas gardé enfermé, et qu’il tue un homme ou une femme, le bœuf sera lapidé, et son propriétaire aussi sera mis à mort.
fr.B: Il en va autrement si le bœuf avait déjà l’habitude d’encorner. Si son propriétaire en avait été averti et ne l’a pas pour autant tenu enfermé, et que le bœuf tue ensuite un homme ou une femme, le bœuf sera lapidé, et le propriétaire aussi sera mis à mort.
fr.R: Mais peut-être que le bœuf a déjà attaqué des gens avec ses cornes, et que le propriétaire a été averti mais ne l’a pas enfermé. Alors, si le bœuf tue un homme ou une femme, il doit être lapidé, et le propriétaire mérite aussi la mort.

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa ng'ombe [alikuwa] na tabia ya kupiga pembe tangu jana [na] siku ya tatu, na mwenyewe ameonywa, naye hakumfunga, naye akamuua mwanamume au mwanamke, ng'ombe huyo atapigwa mawe, na mwenyewe pia atauawa.
sw.B: Ni tofauti ikiwa ng'ombe huyo alijulikana kupiga watu pembe tangu zamani. Ikiwa mwenyewe alikuwa ameonywa kuhusu hatari hiyo lakini bado hakumfungia, naye akamuua mwanamume au mwanamke, ng'ombe huyo atapigwa mawe, na mwenyewe pia atauawa.
sw.R: Lakini huenda ng'ombe huyo amekwisha kuwashambulia watu kwa pembe zake hapo awali, na mwenyewe alionywa lakini hakumfungia. Basi akimuua mwanamume au mwanamke, lazima ng'ombe huyo apigwe mawe, na mwenyewe pia anastahili kufa.

decisions.choice: from yesterday and the third day: in the past
decisions.reason: The phrase means "before now", here in the time before this attack (compare 4:10; 5:7).

decisions.choice: its owner was warned and did not keep it in: guilt through negligence
decisions.reason: The owner knew the danger and did nothing, so he shares the guilt for the death. Verse 30 allows a ransom in his case, since he did not intend to kill.

source.text: אִם־כֹּ֖פֶר יוּשַׁ֣ת עָלָ֑יו וְנָתַן֙ פִּדְיֹ֣ן נַפְשׁ֔וֹ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־יוּשַׁ֖ת עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: If a ransom is laid on him, then he will give the redemption of his life according to all that is laid on him.

en.L: If a ransom is laid on {{gender:them|him}}, then {{gender:they|he}} will give the redemption of {{gender:their|his}} life, according to all that is laid on {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: But if the owner is offered a ransom instead, {{gender:their|his}} life can be redeemed by paying the full amount that is set.
en.R: But the owner may be allowed to pay a price instead. Then the owner must pay all that is asked, and the owner's life will be spared.

es.L: Si se le impone un rescate, dará el precio del rescate de su vida, conforme a todo lo que se le imponga.
es.B: Pero si en lugar de eso se le ofrece al dueño un rescate, podrá rescatar su vida pagando toda la suma que se fije.
es.R: Pero tal vez se le permita al dueño pagar un precio en lugar de morir. Entonces tiene que pagar todo lo que se le pida, y se le perdonará la vida.

fr.L: Si une rançon lui est imposée, il donnera le rachat de sa vie selon tout ce qui lui sera imposé.
fr.B: Mais si l’on propose plutôt au propriétaire une rançon, il pourra racheter sa vie en payant la totalité de la somme fixée.
fr.R: Mais on peut aussi permettre au propriétaire de payer un prix à la place. Alors il doit payer tout ce qu’on lui demande, et sa vie sera épargnée.

sw.L: Ikiwa fidia itawekwa juu yake, basi atatoa ukombozi wa uhai wake, kulingana na yote atakayowekewa.
sw.B: Lakini mwenye ng'ombe akipewa nafasi ya kulipa fidia badala yake, anaweza kukomboa uhai wake kwa kulipa kiasi chote kilichowekwa.
sw.R: Lakini huenda mwenye ng'ombe akaruhusiwa kulipa gharama badala ya kufa. Basi lazima alipe yote anayoambiwa, na uhai wake utaachwa.

decisions.choice: ransom; redemption of his life: a payment that saves his life
decisions.reason: A ransom is a price paid in place of a life. It is allowed here because the owner did not mean to kill. No ransom may be taken for a murderer (Numbers 35:31).

decisions.choice: is laid on him: set by others
decisions.reason: The verse does not say who sets the ransom: perhaps the dead person's family, perhaps the judges (compare verse 22).

source.text: אוֹ־בֵ֥ן יִגָּ֖ח אוֹ־בַ֣ת יִגָּ֑ח כַּמִּשְׁפָּ֥ט הַזֶּ֖ה יֵעָ֥שֶׂה לּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Or a son it gores or a daughter it gores, according to the judgment this it will be done to him.

en.L: Whether it gores a son or gores a daughter, according to this judgment it will be done to {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: If the ox gores a boy or a girl, the owner is dealt with by this same ruling.
en.R: The same law is used if the ox kills a child, boy or girl.

es.L: Ya sea que cornee a un hijo o cornee a una hija, conforme a este juicio se le hará.
es.B: Si el buey cornea a un niño o a una niña, al dueño se le aplicará esta misma norma.
es.R: La misma ley vale si el buey mata a un niño o a una niña.

fr.L: Qu’il encorne un fils ou qu’il encorne une fille, selon ce jugement il lui sera fait.
fr.B: Si le bœuf encorne un garçon ou une fille, le propriétaire sera traité selon cette même règle.
fr.R: On applique la même loi si le bœuf tue un enfant, garçon ou fille.

sw.L: Akimpiga pembe mwana au akimpiga pembe binti, atatendewa kulingana na hukumu hii.
sw.B: Ng'ombe akimpiga pembe mvulana au msichana, mwenye ng'ombe atatendewa kwa agizo hilo hilo.
sw.R: Sheria hiyo hiyo inatumika ng'ombe akimuua mtoto, awe mvulana au msichana.

decisions.choice: a son or a daughter: a child
decisions.reason: The law covers children as well as adults. "To him" is the owner: he, not any child of his, bears the penalty (compare Deuteronomy 24:16).

decisions.choice: judgment: ruling
decisions.reason: The same word as in verse 1. The ruling of verses 28-30 applies.

source.text: אִם־עֶ֛בֶד יִגַּ֥ח הַשּׁ֖וֹר א֣וֹ אָמָ֑ה כֶּ֣סֶף׀שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שְׁקָלִ֗ים יִתֵּן֙ לַֽאדֹנָ֔יו וְהַשּׁ֖וֹר יִסָּקֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: If a male slave gores the ox or a female slave, silver thirty shekels he will give to his master, and the ox will be stoned.

en.L: If the ox gores a male slave or a female slave, [the owner] will give silver, 30 shekels, to [the slave's] master, and the ox will be stoned.
en.B: When the victim is a slave, man or woman, the ox's owner pays {{units:about 12 ounces of silver|30 shekels of silver}} to the slave's master, and the ox is stoned.
en.R: If the ox kills a slave, man or woman, the owner must pay the slave's master {{units:about 12 ounces of silver|30 shekels of silver}}. And the ox must be stoned.

es.L: Si el buey cornea a un esclavo o a una esclava, [el dueño] dará plata, treinta siclos, al amo [del esclavo], y el buey será apedreado.
es.B: Cuando la víctima sea un esclavo o una esclava, el dueño del buey pagará {{units:unos 345 gramos de plata|treinta siclos de plata}} al amo del esclavo, y el buey será apedreado.
es.R: Si el buey mata a un esclavo o a una esclava, el dueño tiene que pagarle al amo del esclavo {{units:unos 345 gramos de plata|treinta siclos de plata}}. Y el buey debe ser apedreado.

fr.L: Si le bœuf encorne un esclave homme ou une esclave femme, [le propriétaire] donnera de l’argent, trente sicles, au maître [de l’esclave], et le bœuf sera lapidé.
fr.B: Si la victime est un esclave, homme ou femme, le propriétaire du bœuf paiera {{units:environ 345 grammes d’argent|trente sicles d’argent}} au maître de l’esclave, et le bœuf sera lapidé.
fr.R: Si le bœuf tue un esclave, homme ou femme, le propriétaire doit payer au maître de l’esclave {{units:environ 345 grammes d’argent|trente sicles d’argent}}. Et le bœuf doit être lapidé.

sw.L: Ikiwa ng'ombe atampiga pembe mtumwa wa kiume au mtumwa wa kike, [mwenye ng'ombe] atampa bwana [wa mtumwa] fedha, shekeli thelathini, naye ng'ombe atapigwa mawe.
sw.B: Ikiwa aliyeuawa ni mtumwa, mwanamume au mwanamke, mwenye ng'ombe atamlipa bwana wa mtumwa {{units:karibu gramu 345 za fedha|shekeli thelathini za fedha}}, na ng'ombe atapigwa mawe.
sw.R: Ng'ombe akimuua mtumwa, mwanamume au mwanamke, lazima mwenye ng'ombe amlipe bwana wa mtumwa huyo {{units:karibu gramu 345 za fedha|shekeli thelathini za fedha}}. Na ng'ombe huyo lazima apigwe mawe.

decisions.choice: thirty shekels of silver: about 12 ounces of silver
decisions.reason: The shekel was a weight, not a coin; coins came much later. A shekel weighed about two-fifths of an ounce (11.5 grams), so thirty shekels was about 12 ounces of silver.

decisions.choice: thirty shekels: the price of a slave
decisions.reason: This sum, paid for a slave's life, became a byword for a low price. In Zechariah 11:12-13 the shepherd is paid thirty pieces of silver, and the priests pay Judas the same to betray Jesus (Matthew 26:15; 27:9-10).

decisions.choice: to his master: the slave as property
decisions.reason: The payment goes to the slave's master for his loss, as for a chattel slave (verse 21). The ox is still stoned, since it has taken a human life.

decisions.choice: {{units:about 12 ounces of silver|30 shekels of silver}}
decisions.reason: Units setting: the modern weight by default, "30 shekels of silver" as the alternative. Literal keeps the shekels. Readable says "kills" for "gores", as the ruling of verses 28-29 is about a death.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought, sold, owned or released: the price is paid to the master for his property (m2, m3).

decisions.choice: {{units:unos 345 gramos de plata|treinta siclos de plata}}
decisions.reason: Units setting as in English: 30 shekels at 11.5 g is about 345 g, the metric default; the shekels are the alternative, and Literal keeps them.

decisions.choice: {{units:environ 345 grammes d’argent|trente sicles d’argent}}
decisions.reason: Units setting as in English: 30 shekels at 11.5 g is about 345 g, the metric default; the shekels are the alternative, and Literal keeps them.

decisions.choice: {{units:karibu gramu 345 za fedha|shekeli thelathini za fedha}}
decisions.reason: Units setting as in English: 30 shekels at 11.5 g is about 345 g, the metric default; the shekels are the alternative, and Literal keeps them.

source.text: וְכִֽי־יִפְתַּ֨ח אִ֜ישׁ בּ֗וֹר א֠וֹ כִּֽי־יִכְרֶ֥ה אִ֛ישׁ בֹּ֖ר וְלֹ֣א יְכַסֶּ֑נּוּ וְנָֽפַל־שָׁ֥מָּה שּׁ֖וֹר א֥וֹ חֲמֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: And when opens a man a pit, or when digs a man a pit and not he covers it, and falls there an ox or a donkey,

en.L: And when {{gender:someone|a man}} opens a pit, or when {{gender:someone|a man}} digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
en.B: Suppose {{gender:someone|a man}} opens up a pit or digs a new one and leaves it without a cover, and an ox or a donkey falls into it.
en.R: {{gender:Someone|A man}} might dig a pit, or open an old one, and not cover it. Then an ox or a donkey might fall in.

es.L: Y cuando {{gender:alguien|un hombre}} abra un pozo, o cuando {{gender:alguien|un hombre}} cave un pozo y no lo cubra, y caiga allí un buey o un asno,
es.B: Supongamos que {{gender:alguien|un hombre}} destapa un pozo o cava uno nuevo y lo deja sin tapar, y un buey o un asno cae en él.
es.R: Puede pasar que {{gender:alguien|un hombre}} cave un pozo, o destape uno viejo, y no lo cubra. Luego un buey o un burro podría caer adentro.

fr.L: Et quand {{gender:quelqu’un|un homme}} ouvre une fosse, ou quand {{gender:quelqu’un|un homme}} creuse une fosse et ne la couvre pas, et qu’un bœuf ou un âne y tombe,
fr.B: Supposons que {{gender:quelqu’un|un homme}} ouvre une fosse ou en creuse une nouvelle sans la couvrir, et qu’un bœuf ou un âne y tombe.
fr.R: Il peut arriver que {{gender:quelqu’un|un homme}} creuse une fosse, ou en ouvre une ancienne, et ne la couvre pas. Puis un bœuf ou un âne peut y tomber.

sw.L: Na mtu akifunua shimo, au mtu akichimba shimo asilifunike, na ng'ombe au punda akaanguka humo,
sw.B: Tuseme mtu amefunua shimo au amechimba jipya na kuliacha bila kifuniko, na ng'ombe au punda akaanguka ndani yake.
sw.R: Huenda mtu akachimba shimo, au akafunua shimo la zamani, asilifunike. Kisha ng'ombe au punda anaweza kuanguka ndani.

decisions.choice: pit: a hole cut in the ground, often a cistern
decisions.reason: The word is used of cisterns for storing water, like the dry pit Joseph was thrown into (Genesis 37:24).

decisions.choice: opens or digs and does not cover: careless with a danger
decisions.reason: Whether the pit is old and reopened or newly dug, the one who leaves it open is responsible for what falls in.

source.text: בַּ֤עַל הַבּוֹר֙ יְשַׁלֵּ֔ם כֶּ֖סֶף יָשִׁ֣יב לִבְעָלָ֑יו וְהַמֵּ֖ת יִֽהְיֶה־לּֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: the owner of the pit will make good; silver he will return to its owner, and the dead will belong to him.

en.L: the owner of the pit will make restitution; silver {{gender:they|he}} will pay back to its owner, and the dead [animal] will be {{gender:theirs|his}}.
en.B: The pit's owner must make good the loss by paying the animal's owner in silver, and may keep the dead animal.
en.R: The owner of the pit must pay the animal's owner for it with money. Then the dead animal belongs to the one who paid.

es.L: el dueño del pozo indemnizará; plata devolverá a su dueño, y el [animal] muerto será suyo.
es.B: El dueño del pozo reparará la pérdida pagando en plata al dueño del animal, y se quedará con el animal muerto.
es.R: El dueño del pozo tiene que pagarle con dinero al dueño del animal. Después, el animal muerto es del que pagó.

fr.L: le propriétaire de la fosse dédommagera ; il rendra de l’argent au propriétaire [de l’animal], et la [bête] morte sera à lui.
fr.B: Le propriétaire de la fosse réparera la perte en payant en argent le propriétaire de l’animal, et il gardera la bête morte.
fr.R: Le propriétaire de la fosse doit payer le propriétaire de l’animal. Ensuite, l’animal mort appartient à celui qui a payé.

sw.L: mwenye shimo atalipa; fedha atamrudishia mwenyewe, na [mnyama] aliyekufa atakuwa wake.
sw.B: Mwenye shimo atalipa hasara kwa kumpa mwenye mnyama fedha, naye atabaki na mnyama aliyekufa.
sw.R: Mwenye shimo lazima amlipe mwenye mnyama pesa. Kisha mnyama aliyekufa ni mali ya yule aliyelipa.

decisions.choice: make restitution: make good the loss in full
decisions.reason: The verb means to make whole, to pay back what was lost. It is used throughout these laws (verses 36-37; 22:2-14).

decisions.choice: the dead will be his: the carcass offsets the payment
decisions.reason: The one who paid keeps the dead animal, whose hide and meat were worth something.

source.text: וְכִֽי־יִגֹּ֧ף שֽׁוֹר־אִ֛ישׁ אֶת־שׁ֥וֹר רֵעֵ֖הוּ וָמֵ֑ת וּמָ֨כְר֜וּ אֶת־הַשּׁ֤וֹר הַחַי֙ וְחָצ֣וּ אֶת־כַּסְפּ֔וֹ וְגַ֥ם אֶת־הַמֵּ֖ת יֶֽחֱצֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: And when strikes the ox of a man the ox of his neighbor and it dies, they will sell the living ox and divide its silver, and also the dead they will divide.

en.L: And when {{gender:someone's|a man's}} ox strikes the ox of {{gender:their|his}} neighbor and it dies, they will sell the living ox and divide its silver, and they will also divide the dead [animal].
en.B: If {{gender:someone's|a man's}} ox injures {{gender:their|his}} neighbor's ox and it dies, they are to sell the ox that is alive and share the price, and share the dead one too.
en.R: If {{gender:someone's|a man's}} ox hurts another person's ox and it dies, the two owners must sell the living ox and split the money. They must also split the dead ox.

es.L: Y cuando el buey de {{gender:alguien|un hombre}} golpee al buey de su prójimo y este muera, venderán el buey vivo y se repartirán su plata, y también se repartirán el [animal] muerto.
es.B: Si el buey de {{gender:alguien|un hombre}} hiere al buey de su vecino y este muere, venderán el buey que está vivo y se repartirán el precio, y se repartirán también el muerto.
es.R: Si el buey de {{gender:alguien|un hombre}} lastima al buey de otra persona y ese buey muere, los dos dueños deben vender el buey vivo y repartirse el dinero. También deben repartirse el buey muerto.

fr.L: Et quand le bœuf {{gender:de quelqu’un|d’un homme}} frappe le bœuf de son prochain et qu’il meurt, ils vendront le bœuf vivant et en partageront l’argent, et ils partageront aussi la [bête] morte.
fr.B: Si le bœuf {{gender:de quelqu’un|d’un homme}} blesse le bœuf de son voisin et que celui-ci meurt, ils vendront le bœuf vivant et se partageront le prix, et ils se partageront aussi la bête morte.
fr.R: Si le bœuf {{gender:de quelqu’un|d’un homme}} blesse le bœuf d’une autre personne et que ce bœuf meurt, les deux propriétaires doivent vendre le bœuf vivant et partager l’argent. Ils doivent aussi partager le bœuf mort.

sw.L: Na ng'ombe wa mtu akimpiga ng'ombe wa jirani yake, naye akafa, watamuuza yule ng'ombe aliye hai na kugawanya fedha yake, na pia watamgawanya yule aliyekufa.
sw.B: Ng'ombe wa mtu akimjeruhi ng'ombe wa jirani yake naye akafa, watamuuza ng'ombe aliye hai na kugawana bei yake, na pia watagawana yule aliyekufa.
sw.R: Ng'ombe wa mtu akimuumiza ng'ombe wa mtu mwingine naye akafa, lazima wenye ng'ombe hao wawili wamuuze ng'ombe aliye hai na kugawana pesa. Lazima pia wagawane ng'ombe aliyekufa.

decisions.choice: they will divide: the loss is shared equally
decisions.reason: Neither owner was at fault, so the two share the loss: each gets half the price of the living ox and half of the dead one.

decisions.choice: strikes: butts or gores
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike or push, here with the horns.

source.text: א֣וֹ נוֹדַ֗ע כִּ֠י שׁ֣וֹר נַגָּ֥ח הוּא֙ מִתְּמ֣וֹל שִׁלְשֹׁ֔ם וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמְרֶ֖נּוּ בְּעָלָ֑יו שַׁלֵּ֨ם יְשַׁלֵּ֥ם שׁוֹר֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשּׁ֔וֹר וְהַמֵּ֖ת יִֽהְיֶה־לּֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Or it is known that an ox prone to gore it [was] from yesterday [and] the third day, and not guarded it its owner, surely he will make good ox in place of the ox, and the dead will belong to him.

en.L: Or [if] it is known that the ox [was] prone to gore from yesterday [and] the third day, and its owner has not kept it in, {{gender:they|he}} will surely make restitution, ox for ox, and the dead [animal] will be {{gender:theirs|his}}.
en.B: But if people knew the ox had a habit of goring and its owner still left it loose, that owner must replace the dead ox with a live one, and the dead one becomes the owner's.
en.R: But if everyone knew the ox had attacked before and the owner did not keep it locked up, the owner must give a living ox to replace the dead one. Then the owner may keep the dead ox.

es.L: O [si] se sabe que el buey [era] dado a cornear desde ayer [y] el tercer día, y su dueño no lo guardó, ciertamente indemnizará buey por buey, y el [animal] muerto será suyo.
es.B: Pero si se sabía que el buey tenía la costumbre de embestir y su dueño aun así lo dejó suelto, ese dueño reemplazará el buey muerto con uno vivo, y el muerto será para él.
es.R: Pero si todos sabían que el buey ya había atacado antes y el dueño no lo mantuvo encerrado, el dueño tiene que dar un buey vivo para reemplazar al muerto. Después puede quedarse con el buey muerto.

fr.L: Ou [s’]il est connu que le bœuf [avait] l’habitude d’encorner depuis hier [et] le troisième jour, et que son propriétaire ne l’a pas gardé enfermé, il dédommagera certainement, bœuf pour bœuf, et la [bête] morte sera à lui.
fr.B: Mais si l’on savait que le bœuf avait l’habitude d’encorner et que son propriétaire l’a quand même laissé en liberté, ce propriétaire remplacera le bœuf mort par un bœuf vivant, et la bête morte lui reviendra.
fr.R: Mais si tout le monde savait que le bœuf avait déjà attaqué et que le propriétaire ne l’a pas enfermé, le propriétaire doit donner un bœuf vivant pour remplacer le bœuf mort. Ensuite, il peut garder le bœuf mort.

sw.L: Au ikijulikana kwamba ng'ombe [alikuwa] na tabia ya kupiga pembe tangu jana [na] siku ya tatu, na mwenyewe hakumfunga, kwa hakika atalipa ng'ombe kwa ng'ombe, na [mnyama] aliyekufa atakuwa wake.
sw.B: Lakini ikiwa ilijulikana kwamba ng'ombe huyo alikuwa na tabia ya kupiga pembe, na bado mwenyewe akamwacha huru, mwenye ng'ombe huyo atalipa ng'ombe aliye hai badala ya yule aliyekufa, na yule aliyekufa atakuwa wake.
sw.R: Lakini ikiwa kila mtu alijua kwamba ng'ombe huyo alishawahi kushambulia, na mwenyewe hakumfungia, lazima mwenyewe atoe ng'ombe aliye hai mahali pa yule aliyekufa. Kisha anaweza kubaki na ng'ombe aliyekufa.

decisions.choice: known to gore and not kept in: the careless owner bears the whole loss
decisions.reason: As in verse 29, the owner knew the danger. He must pay a whole ox for the one killed, keeping the dead animal.

source.text: כִּ֤י יִגְנֹֽב־אִישׁ֙ שׁ֣וֹר אוֹ־שֶׂ֔ה וּטְבָח֖וֹ א֣וֹ מְכָר֑וֹ חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה בָקָ֗ר יְשַׁלֵּם֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשּׁ֔וֹר וְאַרְבַּע־צֹ֖אן תַּ֥חַת הַשֶּֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: When steals a man an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, five cattle he will repay in place of the ox, and four sheep in place of the sheep.

en.L: When {{gender:someone|a man}} steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, five cattle {{gender:they|he}} will repay for the ox, and four sheep for the sheep.
en.B: If {{gender:someone|a man}} steals an ox or a sheep and butchers it or sells it, the thief must replace the ox with five cattle and the sheep with four sheep.
en.R: If {{gender:someone|a man}} steals an ox or a sheep and kills it or sells it, the thief must give back five cattle for one ox, and four sheep for one sheep.

es.L: Cuando {{gender:alguien|un hombre}} robe un buey o una oveja y lo degüelle o lo venda, cinco reses pagará por el buey, y cuatro ovejas por la oveja.
es.B: Si {{gender:alguien|un hombre}} roba un buey o una oveja y lo sacrifica o lo vende, el ladrón restituirá cinco reses por el buey y cuatro ovejas por la oveja.
es.R: Si {{gender:alguien|un hombre}} roba un buey o una oveja y lo mata o lo vende, el ladrón tiene que devolver cinco reses por un buey, y cuatro ovejas por una oveja.

fr.L: Quand {{gender:quelqu’un|un homme}} vole un bœuf ou un mouton et l’abat ou le vend, il rendra cinq bovins pour le bœuf, et quatre moutons pour le mouton.
fr.B: Si {{gender:quelqu’un|un homme}} vole un bœuf ou un mouton et l’abat ou le vend, le voleur remplacera le bœuf par cinq bovins et le mouton par quatre moutons.
fr.R: Si {{gender:quelqu’un|un homme}} vole un bœuf ou un mouton et le tue ou le vend, le voleur doit rendre cinq bovins pour un bœuf, et quatre moutons pour un mouton.

sw.L: Mtu akiiba ng'ombe au kondoo na kumchinja au kumuuza, atalipa ng'ombe watano badala ya yule ng'ombe, na kondoo wanne badala ya yule kondoo.
sw.B: Mtu akiiba ng'ombe au kondoo na kumchinja au kumuuza, mwizi atarudisha ng'ombe watano mahali pa ng'ombe huyo, na kondoo wanne mahali pa kondoo huyo.
sw.R: Mtu akiiba ng'ombe au kondoo, kisha akamchinja au akamuuza, lazima mwizi alipe ng'ombe watano kwa ng'ombe mmoja, na kondoo wanne kwa kondoo mmoja.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: Hebrew 21:37 is 22:1 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does, where chapter 21 has 37 verses. Many Bibles begin chapter 22 with this verse, so 21:37 here is 22:1 there, and 22:1-30 here is 22:2-31 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: five for an ox, four for a sheep: repayment many times over
decisions.reason: A thief who has already killed or sold the animal pays it back many times over; if it is found alive, he pays double (22:3). The ox, a working animal, costs more. David's verdict on the rich man (2 Samuel 12:6) and Zacchaeus's promise (Luke 19:8) both speak of paying back fourfold.

decisions.choice: sheep: one animal of the flock
decisions.reason: The first word means a single sheep or goat; the second, the flock. Both may include goats.
